newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Six firms oppose BellTel petition in Manila.
newsitem.headline: Six firms oppose BellTel petition in Manila.

text.p: Six Philippine telephone companies have asked the National Telecommunications Commission (NTC) to dismiss Bell Telecommunications Philippines (BellTel) bid to operate a nationwide telephone system, the NTC (NTC) on Monday.
These firms were Globe Telecom, Isla Communications Co Inc (Islacom), Philippine Global Communications (Philcom), Eastern Telecommunications Phils Inc, Smart Communications Co Inc and ICC Telecoms.
"This will violate the service area scheme...," the carriers said pointing out that granting BellTel's petition was "anti-business."
Under the service area scheme, the Philippines was divided into 11 service areas with each carrier assigned a particular area.
NTC head Simeon Kintanar told reporters that the NTC will decide BellTel's application within the week.
BellTel in 1993 sought a permit to offer nationwide phone services. Two of three NTC commissioners except Kintanar had earlier approved the application.

The Supreme Court in a decision last May upheld Bell Telecom's contention that the NTC was a collegial body and that an earlier decision by the regulatory body favouring BellTel should have been upheld.
